question:
A hypothetical endothermic reaction is given below:
$$\text{A(g)} + \text{B(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{AB(g)}$$
The activation energy for the reverse reaction is $50\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.
Which ONE of the following is possible for the reaction above?

A The heat of the reaction is $+70\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.
B The activation energy for the forward reaction is $50\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.
C The energy of the activated complex is $40\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.
D The activation energy for the forward reaction is $40\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$.
memo:
A $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: For an endothermic reaction, $\Delta H > 0$ and $E_{a(\text{forward})} - E_{a(\text{reverse})} = \Delta H$. Since $E_{a(\text{forward})} > E_{a(\text{reverse})} = 50\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$, $E_{a(\text{forward})}$ cannot be 40 or 50. $\Delta H = +70\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$ is completely possible (which would correspond to $E_{a(\text{forward})} = 120\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$).*

The concentration of each of the four solutions below is $0{,}1\text{ mol}\cdot\text{dm}^{-3}$:
$$\text{HNO}_3\text{(aq)},\ \text{NH}_3\text{(aq)},\ \text{NaOH(aq) and }\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(aq)}$$
Which ONE of the following CORRECTLY places the solutions in order of INCREASING pH?

A $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\ ;\ \text{HNO}_3\ ;\ \text{NH}_3\ ;\ \text{NaOH}$
B $\text{HNO}_3\ ;\ \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\ ;\ \text{NH}_3\ ;\ \text{NaOH}$
C $\text{NaOH}\ ;\ \text{NH}_3\ ;\ \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\ ;\ \text{HNO}_3$
D $\text{HNO}_3\ ;\ \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\ ;\ \text{NaOH}\ ;\ \text{NH}_3$
memo:
B $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: $\text{HNO}_3$ is a strong acid (lowest pH $\approx 1$), $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a weak acid ($1 < \text{pH} < 7$), $\text{NH}_3$ is a weak base ($7 < \text{pH} < 13$), and $\text{NaOH}$ is a strong base (highest pH $\approx 13$). In order of increasing pH: $\text{HNO}_3 < \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 < \text{NH}_3 < \text{NaOH}$.*

question:
A galvanic cell consists of the following half-cells:
$$\text{Fe}^{3+}\text{(aq)}|\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Ni}^{2+}\text{(aq)}|\text{Ni(s)}$$
Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT for this cell?

A $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is reduced and $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is oxidised.
B $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is oxidised and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is reduced.
C Pt is the electrode at the cathode.
D Ni is the electrode at the cathode.
memo:
C $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: $E^\circ(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}) = +0{,}77\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{Ni}^{2+}/\text{Ni}) = -0{,}27\text{ V}$. $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is the stronger oxidising agent and is reduced at the cathode: $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}$. Because both ions in the cathode half-cell are aqueous, an inert platinum (Pt) electrode is used at the cathode.*
